_about: Everything the app knows about home problems. Costs are typical US national ranges from the public cost guides linked in each entry (checked November 2026). Local prices vary; they are a sanity check, not a quote.

issues.name: Water stain or leak in a ceiling or wall
issues.short: water is getting in from somewhere above or behind the stain
photo_cues: a brown or yellow water stain on a ceiling
a damp water stain spreading on a wall
water damage and discoloration on drywall
issues.symptoms: brown or yellow stain on the ceiling or wall, ring-shaped mark, damp spot, bubbling paint, drip from the ceiling, stain under a bathroom or near a roof
issues.trade: a plumber or roofer to find and stop the leak, then a drywall pro for the stain
issues.diy: Find and fix the source first. Painting over a stain before the leak is fixed hides the problem.
now: Check what's directly above the stain: a bathroom, a pipe, the roof or an AC unit.
Mark the edge of the stain with a pencil and check again in a day to see if it's growing.
If it's dripping, put a bucket under it and turn off the water to that bathroom if you can.

tiers.name: Larger water damage restoration (drying, removal, rebuild)

questions: Where is the water coming from, and how did you confirm it?
Will you check for mold behind the drywall before closing it up?
Is the leak repair and the drywall repair priced separately?
issues.tell_apart: Is the spot wet or growing (a leak), or dry and unchanged for months (an old stain)?

issues.name: Leaking pipe, faucet or drain
issues.short: a pipe, fitting or drain is leaking
photo_cues: a leaking pipe under a sink
water dripping from a pipe joint
a puddle under a sink cabinet with wet pipes
issues.symptoms: dripping pipe, leak under the sink, puddle under the cabinet, wet cabinet floor, leaking faucet, water heater leaking, toilet leaking at the base
issues.diy: A loose drain nut or worn faucet washer is often a simple DIY fix. Leaks from supply lines, the water heater or inside walls need a plumber.
now: Turn off the shut-off valve under the sink or toilet, or the main water valve if it's spraying.
Put a bucket or towels under it and dry the cabinet so you can see where the water starts.
questions: What part failed, and are you replacing just that part or the whole line?
Is there a trip or service-call fee on top of the labor?
Do you guarantee the repair, and for how long?
issues.tell_apart: Can you see water coming from a pipe or fitting, or only a stain on a surface?

issues.name: Mold growth
issues.short: mold is growing because the area stays damp
photo_cues: black mold spots on a wall
mold growing in a bathroom corner
fuzzy green or black mold on a ceiling
issues.symptoms: black, green or white spots, fuzzy patches, musty smell, mold in the bathroom, mold in the corner of the ceiling, mold behind furniture, mildew
issues.trade: a mold remediation specialist for anything larger than about 10 square feet, and a plumber or roofer if a leak is feeding it
issues.diy: Small surface spots (under about 10 square feet) on hard surfaces can usually be cleaned with detergent and water. Larger patches, mold that keeps returning, or mold after a leak need a professional.
now: Open a window or run the bathroom fan to dry the area.
Don't dry-brush or sand it: that spreads spores.
Look for the moisture source: a leak, condensation, or poor ventilation.
questions: What's causing the moisture, and is fixing it included?
How many square feet are affected, and will you test behind the wall?
Will you contain the area so spores don't spread during removal?
issues.tell_apart: Is it fuzzy or spotty and smells musty (mold), or a flat brown ring (a water stain)?

issues.name: Crack in a wall or ceiling
issues.short: a crack in drywall, plaster or concrete, often from normal settling
photo_cues: a thin crack in a concrete surface
a hairline crack in a plaster wall
a crack running through a wall surface
issues.symptoms: hairline crack, crack above a door or window, crack in the drywall, crack in the ceiling, crack in plaster, crack in concrete
issues.trade: a drywall or plaster pro for cosmetic cracks; a structural engineer if it's growing or doors start sticking
issues.diy: Hairline cracks in drywall or plaster are usually cosmetic and can be patched with joint compound and paint.
now: Measure the width and mark both ends with a pencil and the date.
Check again in a few weeks: a crack that grows or widens needs a professional look.
questions: Is this cosmetic, or a sign of movement that will come back?
Will you tape the crack, not just fill it, so it doesn't reopen?
issues.tell_apart: Is it a thin straight crack in drywall or plaster, or a stair-step crack in brick or block?
issues.phrase: a crack in a wall or ceiling

issues.name: Stair-step or foundation crack
issues.short: a crack in brick, block or a foundation wall that can be a sign of movement
photo_cues: a stair-step crack in a brick wall
a zigzag crack along mortar joints in a block wall
a crack in a basement foundation wall
issues.symptoms: stair-step crack in brick, zigzag crack in mortar, crack in the basement wall, foundation crack, crack in block wall, water coming through a foundation crack
issues.trade: a foundation repair company, or a structural engineer first for an independent opinion
issues.diy: Not a DIY job beyond monitoring. A structural engineer's opinion first helps you judge a foundation company's quote.
now: Measure the width and mark both ends with the date. Photograph it with a coin for scale.
Check whether doors or windows nearby have started sticking.
Get an independent structural engineer's opinion before agreeing to a large repair.

tiers.name: Seal or inject a crack
tiers.source: This Old House, foundation crack filling

questions: What's causing the movement, and does your repair address the cause?
Can I see the engineer's report or your measurements?
Is the warranty transferable if I sell the house?
issues.tell_apart: Does the crack follow the mortar lines like stairs, and is it wider than about 1/8 inch?

issues.name: Peeling or bubbling paint
issues.short: paint losing its grip, often from moisture or poor surface prep
photo_cues: paint peeling off a wall
flaking and bubbling paint on a ceiling
chipped paint peeling in strips
issues.symptoms: peeling paint, flaking paint, bubbling paint, blistering paint, paint coming off, chipping paint on the wall or ceiling
issues.trade: a painter, or a DIY job
issues.diy: Usually DIY: scrape loose paint, sand the edges, prime and repaint. If it's in a damp spot, fix the moisture first or it will peel again. In homes built before 1978, test for lead before scraping or sanding.
now: Check for moisture: is it in a bathroom, under a window, or near a stain?
If the home was built before 1978, don't sand or scrape until you've tested for lead paint.
questions: Will you fix the cause (moisture, missing primer) or just repaint?
Is surface prep (scraping, priming) included in the price?
issues.tell_apart: Is the paint flaking off a dry wall, or bubbling over a damp or stained spot (a leak)?

issues.name: Damaged or missing roof shingles
issues.short: shingles are damaged, lifted or missing, so the roof can let water in
photo_cues: missing shingles on a roof
damaged and curling asphalt shingles
a roof with storm damage
issues.symptoms: missing shingles, shingles blew off, curling shingles, granules in the gutter, storm damage on the roof, roof leak, light through the attic
issues.diy: Not recommended: working on a roof is a common cause of serious falls. Look from the ground with binoculars and call a roofer.
now: Look from the ground or a window. Don't climb onto the roof.
Check the attic or top-floor ceilings for damp spots after rain.
If water is coming in, ask a roofer for an emergency tarp.
questions: How many shingles need replacing, and will they match?
Did you check the flashing and underlayment, not just the shingles?
If it's storm damage, will you document it for an insurance claim?
issues.tell_apart: Can you see shingles missing or lifted from the outside, or only a stain on a ceiling inside?

issues.name: Damaged, scorched or warm electrical outlet
issues.short: an outlet or its wiring is overheating or damaged
photo_cues: a scorched electrical outlet with burn marks
a melted wall socket
a cracked electrical outlet cover
issues.symptoms: outlet is warm, scorch marks on the outlet, melted outlet, outlet sparks, buzzing outlet, outlet stopped working, loose plug, burning smell near an outlet
issues.diy: Not a DIY job if it's warm, scorched, sparking or buzzing: those point to wiring problems. A licensed electrician should check it.
now: Unplug everything from it and stop using it.
Turn off its circuit breaker if you can do that safely.
Call an electrician today. If you see smoke or flames, leave and call 911.
questions: What caused it to overheat, and did you check the wiring and the box?
Are other outlets on the same circuit at risk?
Is a permit or inspection needed for this repair?
issues.tell_apart: Is the outlet warm, discolored or sparking, or has it just stopped working?
issues.phrase: a damaged or overheating electrical outlet

hazards.title: Possible gas leak: leave now
steps: Leave the house now and get everyone out.
Don't switch lights on or off, use the phone inside, or start a car in the garage.
Once outside, call 911 or your gas company's emergency line.

hazards.title: Electrical fire risk: stop using it
steps: If there's smoke or flames, leave the house and call 911.
Otherwise turn off the circuit breaker for that area if you can do it safely, and unplug nothing that's hot.
Don't use that outlet or switch until a licensed electrician has checked it.

hazards.title: Water near electricity: turn off the power
steps: Don't touch the fixture, outlet or any water near it.
Turn off the breaker for that area if you can reach the panel without standing in water.
Turn off the water supply, then call an electrician and a plumber.

hazards.title: The ceiling could come down: stay out from under it
steps: Keep everyone and pets out of the room.
Turn off the water to that area or the main valve.
Put a bucket under the low point and call a plumber or water damage company now.

hazards.title: Carbon monoxide alarm: get out
steps: Get everyone outside into fresh air now.
Don't go back in until responders say it's safe.

hazards.title: Sewage backup: avoid contact
steps: Keep children and pets away and don't touch the water without gloves and boots.
Stop using sinks, toilets and appliances that drain.
Call a plumber now; soaked materials usually need professional cleanup.
